doc.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997

title: How Noto got the Kenton job
summary: A bus accident hurt Kenton's trumpeters in Buffalo and Noto was called to fill in.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Sam, how did the thing with Kenton come about?

That was another strange story. I mean a bus had an accident on the Pennsylvania Turnpike coming to Buffalo to perform. And when they got to Buffalo, Conte Candoli and a few other brass players had hit the seat in front you know, and they wiped their chops out. And Conte’s wife was pregnant and she cracked her back, her vertebra, and so he had to leave the band. When they got to Buffalo they needed two trumpet players, so I got the call because I could play high notes. They called the union, you know, said, “You got somebody that can play high?” “Well I mean he gets high, but I don’t know.” Georgie Hobni, you know a black trumpet player in town, we played on the concert that night, and Buddy Childers was the first trumpet player, and we had a little rehearsal in the basement of the theater and then Stan came up and asked, “How’d he do?” He said, “Well he read the chart and everything’s fine.” So he says, “You want to go on the road for a few weeks until Conte comes back?” I said, “Sure.” So I went out and Conte decided not to come back and called Stan and said he was going to stay in California. So that’s how I stayed on the band. It’s a weird way to get on the band, but you know, that’s the way it happened.
Stranger things than that have happened.
